heroHeadline: Day 9,003 of America's Longest War — Op Ghazab Day 96; 27-Day Strike Pause; Eid al-Adha Now Imminent; Russia-Taliban Pact Analysis Published; Jawid Niazi Day 26 in Taliban GDI; UNAMA Mandate Extended
heroSubtitle: June 1, 2026 marks Day 9,003 since the US launched Operation Enduring Freedom on October 7, 2001. Day 96 of Pakistan's Operation Ghazab lil-Haq continues with no confirmed cross-border airstrikes for a 27th consecutive day since the May 5 Dangam (Kunar) strike. Eid al-Adha 2026 is now imminent — the first day of Eid is expected around June 5–6 pending Saudi Arabia's official moon sighting, placing TTP leader Noor Wali Mehsud's announced 3-day ceasefire (10th–12th Dhu al-Hijjah) hours away from activation. Special Eurasia published a strategic analysis on June 1 of the Russia-Taliban Military-Technical Cooperation Agreement signed on May 27-28, noting Russia becomes the first major power to formalize a bilateral defense pact with Taliban-ruled Afghanistan — a paradox given Moscow simultaneously cites Afghanistan as 'evolving into a terror exporter' (per UN/FSB data, May 30). Paigard News Agency director Jawid Niazi remains in Taliban GDI custody on Day 26 — no bail, no charges, no confirmed legal access. TOLOnews journalists Mansoor Niazi and Imran Danish remain on bail pending trial after Eid. UNAMA's mandate was extended by the UN Security Council through June 17, 2026. No Urumqi Round 2 date announced; China silent on mediation since April 8. WFP urgently needs $313M as 4.9M Afghan mothers and children face malnutrition.
